# Connect an agent

::: {.doc-lead}
Connect Claude Code or Codex, check the setup, and start working in a project.
:::

**flux-connect** brings an agent up to speed on Flux, your preferences and a project.
It gives the agent a reading plan and asks it to confirm what it read and saw, then
wait for your instructions. Use Claude Code, Codex, or another agent in its own app
or your preferred terminal. Flux includes the tools, skills and context they need.
Click **AI** in the title bar, or use **Ctrl+K** → **AI status**, to open the monitor.
**Pin** moves the same panel into its own window; **Dock** brings it back.

## Connect Claude Code or Codex {#connect-claude-code-or-codex}

Click **Connect** on the agent's card. Flux installs its skill, registers its MCP
server and installs supported refresh hooks. A replacement shows the exact before
and after text for your confirmation. Flux preserves unrelated settings and keeps
backups. Restart open agent sessions afterward. In Codex, review and trust new
hooks in **/hooks**.

Copy the command on the card into your agent: `/flux-connect <project path>` for
Claude Code, or `$flux-connect <project path>` for Codex. With no project open,
the command uses `global` to introduce Flux and your user context.
**Other agents…** gives manual MCP instructions.

**Repair** checks and repairs the same integration. **Disconnect** removes only
Flux-owned integration and restores prior registrations where safe; edited skills
are kept. Your projects stay available. Connecting or repairing another app's
configuration always starts with your click.

## Set up from a terminal {#set-up-from-a-terminal}

The same setup is available through the [installed launcher](/docs/cli.html):

```bash
flux connect setup --dry-run
flux connect setup
flux connect doctor
```

Use `--agents claude,codex` to choose vendors. Setup preserves unrelated configuration
and backs up changed files; `--yes` confirms replacement of an existing Flux registration.
`--use-this-install` explicitly chooses the launcher owner. `flux connect remove --agents
codex --yes` disconnects that vendor without removing the shared launcher.

For another agent, give it the **Other agents…** MCP configuration, or ask it to run
`flux-connect /path/to/project` (equivalently `flux connect /path/to/project`) in its shell
and follow the printed reading plan. The MCP route provides tools to read the pack and
images even when the agent's shell cannot access the cache.

## What the agent reads {#what-the-agent-reads}

Default connection depth is `core`:

- The short Flux primer and connection contract.
- Your UserContext text; your reference images and skills are indexed for use when needed.
- ProjectContext and its directly linked files, project Rules, and the recent Log with
  an index of all entry titles.
- A project map of documents, figures, decks and plots, open inbox items, and recent activity.
- Rendered canvas overviews so the agent can see the figures.

FluxLib is introduced by its purpose, location and tools; connect does not summarize
your papers. Task manuals and other project documents are indexed for reading on demand.
Large linked files may be shortened; the brief reports omissions and rendering problems.
`--depth full` includes all documents and Log entries, follows project-context links
more deeply, and adds individual figure images and deck contact sheets.

The command returns a **brief**, a short reading plan. The **bundle** holds the text;
together with the rendered images and manifest, it forms a cached **pack**. The agent's
receipt names the project and pack, states what it read and saw, lists open items, and
ends with **Ready.** Its **Proof:** line repeats codes from the ends of bundle sections
and image corners. Check a receipt with `flux connect --check-receipt <packId> "<proof line>"`.
A receipt should acknowledge anything it could not read or view.

Connect is passive: it does not start editing, watching the inbox, or writing the Log.
Give the agent its task after the receipt. See [Annotations, comments and the inbox](/docs/comments.html)
for the review loop and [Your context and your project's](/docs/context.html) for what to maintain.

## Global connection, refresh and live pairing {#global-connection-refresh-and-live-pairing}

Use `/flux-connect global`, `$flux-connect global`, or `flux-connect global` to introduce
Flux and your personal context without choosing a project. It also lists known projects.
An already-bound MCP session keeps its project binding when you connect globally.

Connected MCP tools add a **↻ Since you last looked** notice when others change the project;
the agent can read the details with `read_delta`. Setup also installs supported prompt hooks
so changes can reach the agent on your next message. Claude Code's hook refreshes automatically;
Codex hooks require the installed version's support and your **/hooks** trust decision.
For a fresh reading plan on demand, ask for `flux connect /path/to/project --refresh`.

Add `--live` when connecting to pair with the open project. The agent checks the current
selection each turn and can use `get_view` when you mean “this” or “what I'm seeing.”
The titlebar briefly shows **◉ heron viewed your window**, using the session's name.
**Settings → General → Allow agents to view the Flux window** controls this access and is
on by default. Capture covers only that project's Flux window. See
[live pairing](/docs/comments.html#pair-with-the-live-window) for handoffs through Annotate.

## Read the status {#read-the-status}

The titlebar dot is green when the bundle is ready for a connected agent, amber
when it needs attention, and red when a connected integration or shared part is
broken. Detected agents that are not connected need attention. Dismissing the
one-time **Connect an AI agent** Home card remembers that choice; it never hides
an actual error.

The panel has four sections:

- **Agents** shows installed versions and each agent's skill, registration,
  responding MCP, published user skills and refresh hook.
- **Bundle** shows the launcher and its owning install, the manual, user context,
  rendering and your Skills.
- **Sessions** shows the agents connected to this project, their watching and live
  badges, queues, current claims and connection times. **Stop watching** releases
  the session's claims and tells its wait loop to stop.
- **This project** shows this window's live bridge, saved inbox counts and last
  connection. Save edits to margin comments to include them in these counts.

Expand a row for its paths, version, last check, error and available fix.
**Run doctor** performs fresh execution checks, including the MCP handshake and a
small figure render, with results as each check finishes. **Copy diagnostics** runs
those checks and copies the doctor JSON. Vendor configuration values are kept out
of status and diagnostics; they appear only in a replacement you are confirming.

The panel paints its cached status immediately. Cheap probes refresh it on open,
after setup and every ten minutes. Full doctor checks run only when requested.
Execution checks say **Not checked** until a doctor result is available.

## Your skills {#your-skills}

In **Bundle → Skills**, click **New skill…**, or use **Ctrl+K** → **New agent skill…**.
Enter a short lowercase name with hyphens, such as `stats-conventions`. Flux creates
a folder with a starter `SKILL.md` and opens it in your default editor, just like
**Open global rules**. Describe when to use the procedure, its steps and checks.

**Reveal in folder** opens the skills location. Skills are published to connected
agents and kept in sync: invoke `/stats-conventions` in Claude Code or
`$stats-conventions` in Codex. **Re-publish** checks publication now. Name collisions
and edited vendor copies are reported and preserved.

## What is the AI bundle? {#what-is-the-ai-bundle}

| Part | What it gives agents | Where it lives | How it gets there |
|---|---|---|---|
| Launcher + `flux` CLI | every verb from any shell | `<binDir>/flux` (+ `flux-connect`) → the app's bundled CLI | written by Flux on every start |
| Flux MCP server | typed tools, images, live tools, inbox, watch | `"<launcher>" mcp` | registered with an agent by **Connect** |
| `flux-connect` skill | the one command | `~/.claude/skills/flux-connect`, `~/.agents/skills/flux-connect` | **Connect** |
| Your skills | `/stats-conventions` anywhere | `UserContext/Skills` → published to each connected agent | **Connect**, then kept in sync |
| Flux manual (FluxContext) | how to use Flux | `<FluxConfig>/Context/FluxContext` | synced by Flux on start |
| Your context (UserContext) | who you are, your rules | `<FluxConfig>/Context/UserContext` | yours (seeded blank) |
| Figure rendering | agents can *see* figures | inside the app bundle | shipped |
| Auto-refresh hook | agents stay current | `~/.claude/settings.json` (managed entry) | **Connect** (Claude Code) |
| Live bridge | selection, live edits, `get_view` | per open project (`.meta/live/`) | automatic while a project is open |
| Project inbox | annotations + comments for agents | per project (`.meta/feedback.ndjson`, comment sidecars) | automatic |

The bundle ships with Flux. **Connect** is the step that registers it with an agent.
See [Annotations, comments and the inbox](/docs/comments.html) for routing and replies,
and [Your context and your project's](/docs/context.html) for the files agents read.

## Troubleshooting {#troubleshooting}

If a row is red, expand it and run **Fix** when offered. **Run doctor** gives the
latest execution evidence. **Use this Flux for agents** explicitly chooses this
installation when the launcher belongs to another checkout or install.

If a new skill does not appear, check its name and description in the frontmatter,
use **Re-publish**, and restart your agent session. Flux leaves edited and unmanaged
files alone; the row explains any collision or permission error.

If no sessions appear, run the copied connection command in the agent. Presence
appears after an explicit project connection and expires when its heartbeat stops.
The monitor does not start an agent or enable watch mode by itself.

If `flux` is not on PATH, use the full launcher path from the [command-line guide](/docs/cli.html#invoking).
Run `flux connect doctor` (or `--json`) for the same diagnostics from a terminal.
If an agent's shell cannot write outside its workspace, use the registered MCP tools;
connect also has a temporary-cache fallback. Setup does not change the agent's sandbox policy.
